def: to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey)

occurrences.text: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
